quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Slow down as you approach, then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach, then speed up and leave it behind.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, slow down as you approach it. Then speed up and ride away. If you see a larger animal, brake and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them without forcing the newer rider to lead the group.

questions.question: A good lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you set up for turns.
Help you avoid wind blasts from other vehicles.
Place you in another vehicle's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place you in another vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. It helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you from behind, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center of your lane.
Stay on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind, stay in the center of your lane. Riding closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane give a motorcyclist?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane gives motorcyclists three paths to travel: the left side, the center, and the right side of the lane.

questions.question: Riders wearing helmets are ________ more likely to survive a crash than those without helmets.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: A helmet makes you three times more likely to survive head injuries in a crash, no matter what speed you are traveling.

questions.question: When braking on a wet or slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Do not brake, but downshift instead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed and avoid sudden movements. If you must slow down or stop, use both brakes.

questions.question: Before a passenger rides your motorcycle, you should tell them to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Get on after the engine has started.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Keep a large distance between themselves and you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a large distance between themselves and you.
questions.explanation: Your passenger should mount after the engine starts. They should sit as close to you as possible without crowding you, and hold onto the handholds or your waist. They should keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and moving parts.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
Press the handle grip opposite to the direction you want to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press slightly on the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then press the right to straighten. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another motorcycle on the left, you should:

options.text: Move to the right side of your lane so they see you in their side mirror.
Move to the left side of your lane to see better ahead.
Stay in the center of your lane so they see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the left side of your lane to see better ahead.
questions.explanation: When passing on the left, ride on the left side of your lane to see the road ahead better and to be more visible. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. They tell you the rules of the road. You must follow these signs.

questions.question: A linked braking system:

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes, applying both brakes when either brake lever is applied.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter, applying the brake when the rider downshifts.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a switch on the handlebar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes, applying both brakes when either brake lever is applied.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake lever, both brakes apply. Check your owner's manual to learn more about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: Which of the following is true?

options.text: The front and rear brakes provide equal braking power.
The front brake provides more braking power than the rear brake.
The rear brake provides more braking power than the front brake.
Only the front brake should be used when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake provides more braking power than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your stopping power. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: About ______ of accidents involve driver inattention?
questions.correctAnswerText: 80 percent
questions.explanation: About 80 percent of crashes happen because drivers are not paying attention.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use abrupt pressure on the front brake to prevent locking the front tire.
Use either brake, but use only one brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the brake lever slowly to avoid locking the front wheel. Use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When packing a load on a motorcycle:

options.text: The heavier items should go toward the front.
The heavier items should go toward the rear.
Mounting loads behind the rear axle is recommended.
Lighter items should be stored in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The heavier items should go toward the front.
questions.explanation: Place heavier items toward the front of your load. Keep the load over or in front of the rear axle. Pack lighter items behind you.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: At the rear of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a possible cause of a wobble on your motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Uneven road
questions.explanation: Wobbles are usually caused by improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not speed up to get out of a wobble.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking alcohol and wants to drive, which of the following should you not do?

options.text: Encourage friends to talk them out of driving.
Tell them to take less-crowded roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to take less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: Do not let someone drive after drinking. Instead, arrange other transportation for them, get friends to help stop them from leaving, or keep them busy to slow their drinking. Do not suggest they take safer routes—they should not drive at all.

questions.question: What should you do on a long trip?

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel sleepy.
Wear warm clothing to protect against cold and wind.
Ride more than 12 hours per day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear warm clothing to protect against cold and wind.
questions.explanation: Protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain to reduce fatigue on long trips. Ride no more than 6 hours per day and take rest breaks at least every 2 hours. Do not use caffeine or other stimulants because you will become very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down or stop
questions.explanation: Riders can use hand signals instead of or with turn signals. When the left arm is bent at the elbow and points downward, it means the rider will slow down or stop.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, you should:

options.text: Speed up before you hit it.
Slow down before you hit it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you hit it.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, try to hit it at a 90-degree angle. Slow down as much as you can before impact. Keep the motorcycle upright, rise slightly off the seat, and ease off the throttle just before impact.

questions.question: How do you regain control if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Swerve toward the side with fewer hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Release the rear brake to regain control of a locked rear wheel. However, if the rear brake locks on a good surface, you can keep it locked until the motorcycle stops completely.

questions.question: Which collision does NOT require a police report?

options.text: A collision that damages property over $1,000
A collision with an unattended vehicle
A minor accident in a parking lot

questions.correctAnswerText: A minor accident in a parking lot
questions.explanation: You must report a collision to police if you hit an unattended vehicle, if someone is injured, or if property damage is over $1,000.
